02 History

Our history

From a school founded on service to a unit that gives the gift of health.

Established April 1972

The gift of health

The name Saukyadana joins two Sinhala words: saukya, meaning health, and dana, meaning giving. The Saukyadana Unit of Ananda College, Colombo 10, established in April 1972, is the college's health and first aid service unit, and it lives by one motto: Live for Lives.

Ananda College itself was founded in 1886 by Colonel Henry Steel Olcott and the Buddhist Theosophical Society, with a mission of education grounded in service to the community. The Saukyadana Unit carries that spirit into health care, first aid and public wellbeing.

The unit's best-known programme is Arogya, an annual inter-school first aid competition and workshop that the unit organises at Ananda College.

Today a new generation of student leaders runs Arogya, Restart Heart, Medica, Health Pulse and Nadiya, along with health camps such as the Sripadha camp and school health camps.

Sources: Ananda College history (Sunday Times, 2021); Arogya 2014 (Daily Mirror, 30 Jan 2014).

1886

Ananda College is founded

Colonel Henry Steel Olcott and the Buddhist Theosophical Society open the school in Colombo.

April 1972

The Saukyadana Unit is established

The Saukyadana Unit of Ananda College is founded, giving students a place to learn first aid and serve others.

Decades of service

Arogya and health camps grow

Over more than fifty years the unit builds Arogya, its annual inter-school first aid programme, and takes health services to schools and communities.

Today

A new generation leads

Ten student leaders run Arogya, Restart Heart, Medica, Health Pulse, Nadiya and health camps under the motto Live for Lives.
